entry.name: Preterite with Present-Time Politeness
entry.pattern: Clause[preterite of a request-related predicate + complement]

1.definition: Softens a present request by presenting it as an already entertained thought or intention.

examples.form: [I wanted to ask] if a seat was available.

projection.target: The request can be made at the time of speaking. The morphology also has a literal past interpretation in a context that supplies a past intention.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Past tense for a polite request now
curious.summary: A past-tense verb can soften a request being made right now.
curious.body:
In I wanted to ask if a seat was available, the person is asking now. The past tense wanted presents the request as a thought or intention they've already had, which softens it.

The same form can also have a literal past meaning, if the situation supplies a past intention. This dictionary marks the account as provisional.

examples.text: [I wanted to ask] if a seat was available.

curious.try: How would you ask for something politely using a past-tense verb? Does it feel gentler than a present-tense version?

teacher.summary: Explains why a past-tense verb can make a present request more polite.
teacher.explain: The preterite of a request-related predicate plus a complement can soften a present request by presenting it as an already entertained thought or intention. In I wanted to ask if a seat was available, the request is made at the time of speaking. The same morphology can also be literally past, in a context that supplies a past intention. This dictionary marks the analysis provisional, so present it as a description of this example, and point out that tense can express more than time.
teacher.terms: Sometimes called the 'past tense of politeness' or 'tentative past'; this dictionary uses preterite for the past tense form.

examples.text: [I wanted to ask] if a seat was available.

watch_for: A learner might take wanted as describing something that happened only in the past.
A learner might not realize the speaker is asking now.
teacher.activity: Students role-play asking for a seat or a favour, first with a plain request and then with a past-tense softened one, and say how each might sound to the listener.
